total Wide open #

Upper bounds — holds for every total

  • \(\text{(conjectured) } \mathrm{MaxInf}(p) \ge \mathrm{poly}\big(\mathrm{Var}(p)/\deg(p)\big) \text{ for bounded } p\)
    AaronsonAmbainis14todo: open
    The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture. A bounded degree-$d$ real polynomial with variance $\ge\varepsilon$ should have a variable of influence $\ge \mathrm{poly}(\varepsilon/d)$.

Consequence if true: $\mathrm{R}(f) = \mathrm{poly}(\mathrm{Q}(f))$ for all total $f$ -- and more generally, every bounded-error quantum query algorithm on a product distribution can be simulated classically with polynomially many queries. This is the main structural conjecture behind "quantum speedups need structure".

see also: \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\), \(\widetilde{\deg}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{R}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{I}^{1}(f)\), The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture data/relations/05-fourier.yaml

facts: $\mathrm{D}(f)\ge \mathrm{Var}(f)/\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)$ (OSSS). Recorded as the measure \(\mathrm{osss}(f)\).
$\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\le\mathrm{Var}(f)$ always, so the ratio above is never below $1$; equality for $\oplus_n$ and for a dictator.
KKL: $\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\ge\Omega(\mathrm{Var}(f)\log n/n)$, so the ratio never exceeds $O(n/\log n)$; \(\mathrm{Tribes}_{w,s}\) attains it.
For a bounded degree-$d$ function, $\mathrm{MaxInf} \ge \mathrm{Var}/(\text{something in } d)$ is the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture -- open.
self.name: Maximum influence

up.note:
The one cell among the normalized quantities that is a genuine bound,
because noise sensitivity dominates maximal influence rather than being
incomparable to it. Writing
$\mathrm{NS}_\delta = \tfrac12\sum_S \big(1-(1-2\delta)^{|S|}\big)\hat f(S)^2$
and keeping only the sets through a fixed coordinate $i$, every such $S$
has $|S| \ge 1$ and hence $1-(1-2\delta)^{|S|} \ge 2\delta$, so
$\mathrm{NS}_\delta(f) \ge \delta \sum_{S \ni i} \hat f(S)^2 = \delta\,\mathrm{Inf}_i(f)$.
Maximise over $i$. The factor $1/\delta$ is exactly right: the dictator
has $\mathrm{MaxInf} = 1$ and $\mathrm{NS}_\delta = \delta$.

lo.note: At fixed $\delta$ the two are within a constant factor on $\oplus_n$, so the exponent is $1$ and the cell closes.

total Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every total

  • \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(f) \le \mathrm{NS}_\delta(f)/\delta \quad (0 \le \delta \le \tfrac12)\)
    ODonnell14
    The one cell among the normalized quantities that is a genuine bound, because noise sensitivity dominates maximal influence rather than being incomparable to it. Writing $\mathrm{NS}_\delta = \tfrac12\sum_S \big(1-(1-2\delta)^{|S|}\big)\hat f(S)^2$ and keeping only the sets through a fixed coordinate $i$, every such $S$ has $|S| \ge 1$ and hence $1-(1-2\delta)^{|S|} \ge 2\delta$, so $\mathrm{NS}_\delta(f) \ge \delta \sum_{S \ni i} \hat f(S)^2 = \delta\,\mathrm{Inf}_i(f)$. Maximise over $i$. The factor $1/\delta$ is exactly right: the dictator has $\mathrm{MaxInf} = 1$ and $\mathrm{NS}_\delta = \delta$.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(\oplus_n) = 1, \qquad \mathrm{NS}_\delta(\oplus_n) \to \tfrac12\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\)
    At fixed $\delta$ the two are within a constant factor on $\oplus_n$, so the exponent is $1$ and the cell closes.
see also: \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\), \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f)\), \(\mathrm{I}(f)\), \(\oplus_n\) data/relations/12-normalized.yaml

total:
total No bound exists #

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(\oplus_n) = 1, \qquad \mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(\oplus_n) = \rho^{\,n} \to 0\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\) ODonnell14
    Maximal influence pinned at its ceiling while noise stability decays geometrically. The genuine bound in this cell is the one in $1 - \mathrm{Stab}$, recorded in the notes.

$$\mathrm{MaxInf}(f) \le \frac{1 - \mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(f)}{1-\rho}$$ is the real content of this cell -- substitute $\delta = (1-\rho)/2$ into the $\mathrm{MaxInf} \le \mathrm{NS}_\delta/\delta$ bound proved at \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\) vs \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f)\). It is a bound in $1 - \mathrm{Stab}$, not in $\mathrm{Stab}$, and no bound $O(\mathrm{Stab}_\rho^k)$ in $\mathrm{Stab}$ itself is possible: $\oplus_n$ has $\mathrm{MaxInf} = 1$ with $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho = \rho^{\,n} \to 0$.

see also: \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(f)\), \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f)\), \(\oplus_n\) data/relations/12-normalized.yaml
